question.value: Whether the presence of H II regions modifies the core-scale (~0.025 pc) fragmentation and star formation in candidate high-mass starless clumps (HMSCs).

evidence.quote: The question of whether the presence of H ii regions modifies the core-scale (∼ 0.025 pc) fragmentation and star formation in HMSCs remains to be explored.
We aim to investigate the difference of 0.025 pc-scale fragmentation between candidate HMSCs that are strongly impacted by H ii regions and less disturbed ones.
We made use of the ALMA data observed in ALMA Cycle 4 by project 2016.1.01346.S
(ACA) in the ALMA Cycle 4 project 2016.1.01346.S.

findings_qualitative.value: Within the sample of eight clumps, there is no clear difference in the ~0.025 pc-scale core mass and separation distributions between H II-region-impacted (AS) and non-impacted (NA) candidate HMSCs.

evidence.quote: We did not find a clear difference in the fragmented ALMA core mass and separations between AS HMSCs and NA HMSCs in our limited sample, although H ii regions seem to affect the morphology of the cores’ spatial distribution.

findings_qualitative.value: Fragmentation in both AS and NA candidate HMSCs is dominated by two-level hierarchical thermal Jeans fragmentation, where clumps fragment into ensembles at ~lambda_J,clump^th and ensembles sub-fragment into cores at ~0.3 lambda_J,clump^th (~1 to 1.5 lambda_J,ens^th).

evidence.quote: Both types of candidate HMSCs present a thermal fragmentation with two-level hierarchical features at the clump thermal Jeans length λ th J,clump and 0.3λ th J,clump .

evidence.loc: Sect. 4.3 Hierarchical fragmentation shown by 7 m data
evidence.quote: As a result, the early-stage fragmentation in the high-mass clumps probably takes place in a hierarchical fashion: clumps fragment into ensembles with separations around clump thermal Jeans length

findings_qualitative.value: No high-mass prestellar cores are found in the sample; the most massive cores (> 8 M_sun) show star-forming signposts such as outflows, shocked/warm gas tracers, or IR point sources.

evidence.quote: The most massive cores ( M core 8 M ⊙ ) in our candidate HMSCs commonly present star-forming signposts, implying that there is no high-mass prestellar core in our sample.

findings_qualitative.value: H II regions shape the spatial distribution of dense gas and dust at ~0.025 pc scale in deeply impacted clumps (cometary globule morphology in AS1 and wall-like core alignment along the ionization front in AS2) and likely assist or induce star formation.

evidence.quote: ALMA continuum reveals that AS1 presents a cometary globular morphology meanwhile the fragmented cores in AS2 show a spatial distribution aligned with the ionization front.

claims.hypothesis: H II region feedback modifies the ~0.025 pc-scale fragmentation (core masses and separations) of associated candidate HMSCs compared to isolated candidate HMSCs of similar clump mass and distance.
claims.experiment: Imaged four pairs of mass- and distance-matched AS and NA candidate HMSCs with ALMA Band 6 (12 m + 7 m) continuum at ~1.3" (~0.025 pc) resolution, extracted cores with Astrodendrograms, and compared core masses and MST separations scaled by clump and ensemble Jeans parameters.
claims.result: 51 cores were detected across the 8 clumps (3 to 9 per clump); scaled core separations S_core/lambda_J,clump^th, ensemble separations S_ens/lambda_J,clump^th, and core masses M_core/M_J,clump^th show no clear difference between AS and NA.
claims.finding: Within this limited sample of 8 clumps, there is no clear difference in the ~0.025 pc-scale fragmentation between impacted and non-impacted candidate HMSCs.

evidence.quote: Within our limited sample, we did not find a clear difference in the ∼ 0.025 pc-scale fragmentation between impacted and non-impacted candidate HMSCs, even though H ii regions seem to affect the spatial distribution of the fragmented cores.

evidence.quote: In this limited statistic, there is no clear overall trend that fragmentation between AS and NA has a significant difference.

claims.hypothesis: Fragmentation in candidate HMSCs at ~0.025 pc scale is governed by hierarchical thermal Jeans fragmentation rather than turbulent Jeans fragmentation.
claims.experiment: Compared core and 7 m ACA ensemble masses and MST separations against thermal, turbulent (total support), and compressible-flow Jeans parameters, and tested the modality of 363 scaled MST core separations across 31 candidate HMSCs.
claims.result: Ensemble separations have a median S_ens/lambda_J,clump^th ~ 1, core separations inside ensembles have a median S_core/lambda_J,ens^th ~ 1–1.5, and the 31-clump scaled separation distribution is bimodal with peaks at 0.38 and 0.9 lambda_J,clump^th (with only AS1 deviating to ~3x thermal values).
claims.finding: Fragmentation from pc-scale clumps to ~0.025 pc cores occurs via two-level hierarchical thermal Jeans fragmentation, favouring competitive accretion over monolithic collapse.

evidence.quote: It is not only core mass, but also core separations that present a hierarchical thermal fragmentation, favouring the CA model for high-mass star formation.
More than 70% of MST separations are less than λ th J,clump . The maximum and sub-maximum are peaked at around 0.38λ th J,clump and 0.9λ th J,clump, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: H II regions can compress and shape dense gas/dust structures down to ~0.025 pc scales and induce star formation in pre-existing candidate HMSCs.
claims.experiment: Compared ALMA 1.3 mm core and 7 m ensemble morphologies and mass-weighted centers with MAGPIS 20 cm free-free emission, Spitzer 8 um PAH emission, and Hi-GAL PPMAP column density profiles, and evaluated collect-and-collapse and RDI timescales.
claims.result: AS2 and AS4 show offsets of core centers toward the H II interface; AS1 displays a cometary globule surrounded by an overpressured 20 cm ionized front with t_frag (~0.9 Myr) > bubble age (~0.4 Myr) and interaction time (0.04–0.13 Myr) matching its age; AS2 cores form a wall-like structure aligned with the 8 um PDR and 20 cm ionization front.
claims.finding: H II regions shape the spatial distribution of dense structures at ~0.025 pc scale in pre-existing clumps (AS1 and AS2) and likely trigger or accelerate core/star formation via radiation-driven implosion and shock compression.

referee_caveats_inferred: Core and ensemble turbulent Jeans parameters at the sub-clump (< 0.1 pc) scale were not directly measured from ALMA molecular line widths, relying instead on single-dish clump line widths (~20-40" beams).
The definition of 7 m ACA 'ensembles' mixes automated Astrodendrogram leaves, manual splitting of elongated leaves by contour subpeaks, and visual addition of low-S/N structures (W1).

AS3 is not truly a starless clump (it hosts a 24 um and 70 um source at ALMA1) and is only weakly impacted by its H II region, reducing the effective strongly-impacted starless sample to three clumps.
